title: Olduvai Gorge
summary: Olduvai Gorge is a 14 km deep ravine in Tanzania, inside the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. Its layers hold a sequence of hominin species and the Oldowan stone tools. Louis and Mary Leakey and their son Jonathan found the first Homo habilis fossils there in 1960, including the partial skeleton of a boy about 1.8 million years old.

uncertainty.note: Converted as year = 1950 minus age. The Natural History Museum gives about 1.8 Ma for the OH 7 partial skeleton and for Oldowan tools, a hammerstone at 1.85-1.6 Ma, and Homo habilis at about 2.0-1.6 Ma; the pin uses 1.8 Ma. UNESCO says the sequence runs up to Homo sapiens, so the gorge as a site spans a longer time.
